study_identification.title: Mapping Neurophysiological Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder Using Normative Models of the Functional Connectome

study_characteristics.study_objective: To identify neurophysiological subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) by quantitatively mapping individual deviations in functional connectome strength from normative lifespan trajectories.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: A k-means clustering algorithm was used to explore MDD subtypes with different deviation patterns. Support vector regression analysis was conducted to examine the predictive ability of baseline deviation values for treatment response in each patient subtype.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study identified two reproducible neurophysiological subtypes of MDD with distinct functional connectome deviation patterns and clinical characteristics.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Two MDD subtypes were identiﬁed based on individual FCS deviations. Subtype 1 (37%, n = 425) showed severe deviations, with positive deviations in the DMN, LIM, and SUB areas and negative deviations in the sensorimotor, dorsal attention, and ventral attention areas, while subtype 2 (63%, n = 723) showed moderate deviations with a conversed deviation pattern. The severe-deviation subtype had more severe symptoms as measured using the suicide item, while the moderate-deviation subtype exhibited more severe symptoms as measured by the work and activities and depressed mood items. The baseline individual deviation map could signiﬁcantly predict HDRS score changes after treatment for the severe-deviation subtype (r = 0.47, p = .019, one-tailed permutation test).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: First, our analysis was performed based on data from a cross-sectional sample... Second, in this study, we compared the subtype differences in clinical symptoms using HDRS-17 item scores. The patients with MDD also had varied cognitive impairments, which were not assessed in the current retrospective study. Third, all the patients who were included in the analysis to predict treatment outcomes were responders to paroxetine... Fourth, although the signiﬁcance level of our results was corrected for multiple comparisons using the FDR method, the effect sizes of subtype differences are relatively small... Fifth, an episode of MDD...
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Our study offers a novel analytical framework for subtyping MDD and offers promising implications for future personalized diagnosis and treatment of this disorder.
